layman_note.what: Built the project skeleton: folders, README, walkthrough, tests, CI, and a frozen 21-step plan.
layman_note.why: Every later step builds on a tested, scope-locked base â€” no drift possible.
layman_note.concept: Scaffold â€” the empty-but-working skeleton built before any real logic, so the project stays green from day one.
layman_note.next: Download the NAB dataset and document what is inside those 58 data streams.

layman_note.what: Downloaded the full NAB dataset (58 CSV streams across 7 categories, plus ground-truth anomaly labels) via a reusable download script.
layman_note.why: The benchmark data is the raw material for everything that follows.
layman_note.concept: Data ingestion â€” writing a script that fetches, organises, and validates a dataset so the pipeline starts from a clean, verified base.
layman_note.next: Implement the NAB scoring protocol so we can actually measure how good (or bad) our detectors are.

layman_note.what: Implemented the NAB scoring protocol with 3 application profiles (standard, reward-low-FP, reward-low-FN) and 29 unit tests.
layman_note.why: The scorer is the ruler that measures every detector we build â€” without it, there is no way to compare our results to the published NAB leaderboard.
layman_note.concept: NAB scoring â€” a scaled sigmoid rewards early detection within an anomaly window and penalises false alarms; scores are normalised so a null detector = 0 and a perfect detector = 100.
layman_note.next: Implement a null detector and verify it scores exactly 0 on the real NAB data â€” validating the scoring pipeline end-to-end.

layman_note.what: Built a null detector (always says 'no anomaly'), a data loader for all 58 NAB streams, and a scoring runner. Null detector scores exactly 0.0 on all 3 profiles â€” validating the full pipeline end-to-end.
layman_note.why: The null baseline proves the scoring pipeline works correctly before we plug in real detectors. Score 0.0 is the mathematical expectation â€” any other number would mean the scorer is broken.
layman_note.concept: Baseline â€” a deliberately simple detector whose expected score is known in advance; if the measured score matches, the pipeline is trustworthy.
layman_note.next: Reproduce at least 1 published NAB baseline score and validate against published numbers.

layman_note.what: Implemented Windowed Gaussian detector with incremental stats and sweep-based threshold optimizer. Reproduced published NAB baseline: standard 40.13 vs published 39.6 (1.4 pct diff), reward_low_fn 22.95 vs published 22.8 (0.7 pct diff).
layman_note.why: Reproducing a published score proves scoring pipeline plus detector match the original benchmark.
layman_note.concept: Windowed Gaussian: slides a fixed-size window, computing mean and std incrementally O(1). Points far from the mean score high via the Q-function tail probability.
layman_note.next: Implement a second detector and compare against the Gaussian baseline.
